Quantum security is this week's main topic.

It was nice seeing @muneeb address the dangers as one of his first priorities as the new CEO.

Here's a TL;DR of his speech from @token2049:

Quantum is one part of his bigger vision for Stacks through 2030, built around three priorities called the "Satoshi Upgrades":

1. Bitcoin capital markets
Earn BTC yield and eventually borrow against that same BTC without giving up custody.

2. Compliant privacy
Keep balances and transactions private, while letting authorized parties like auditors see what they need.

3. Post-quantum security
Prepare Stacks for future quantum threats before they become a serious concern for Bitcoin holders.

There's already progress on the first front, with the Bitcoin Staking Genesis Bond selling out at 230 BTC in September and PoX-6 targeted for 2027 to open participation beyond the current whitelist.

There's a lot left to build, but kudos to the @Stacks team for trying to make BTC more useful while keeping custody and settlement tied to Bitcoin.

Disclosure: I'm an $STX holder and Stacks supporter.

📊 DAILY METALS PULSE — WEEKLY WRAP
📅 Friday, 9 October 2026

A volatile week, with gold, silver and copper finding buyers again on Friday.

☢️ URANIUM
Kazatomprom shareholders approved a uranium contract with China’s SNURDC, while the proposed Uranium One contract failed after 88.34% abstained. My take: another reminder of why diversified, secure fuel supplies matter to the nuclear industry.

🔌 COPPER
China’s return from Golden Week and the strike at Chile’s Centinela mine brought demand and supply risks back into focus. London copper was heading for a weekly gain, with mine disruptions supporting prices despite macro headwinds.

🥇 GOLD
Gold recovered toward $4,200/oz, heading for roughly a 1.3% weekly gain after Wednesday’s two-month low. Buyers returned, although elevated yields and the risk of further Fed hikes remain headwinds.

🌍 NEXT WEEK
US inflation data is the next major test for rate expectations and precious metals. Friday’s rebound gives bulls something to build on.

I remain focused on the longer-term opportunity: secure uranium supplies, copper for electrification, and precious metals in an uncertain macro environment. Let’s see whether Friday’s buying carries into next week.

tweets.text:
What can you actually do with a tokenized stock right now?

Mostly hold it and trade it. Almost all of the products people actually use around stocks still live inside banks.

Structured notes are a good example. 

They're products that pay you a regular coupon as long as a stock doesn't fall too far, and banks issued roughly $538B of callable structured notes last year. 

However, there’s basically no real onchain version of that market.

@notesystems is trying to turn that desk into a protocol on Robinhood Chain.

The easiest way to understand it is that a structured note is basically matching two different needs.

• One side of users has stablecoins and wants yield.
• The other side already owns a stock and wants protection if it falls hard.

Normally, a bank sits between them. Note Systems replaces that middle layer with smart contracts.

The stablecoin side deposits USDG and earns a coupon while the stock stays above a set barrier. The stock holder pays those coupons and gets downside protection without selling.

Everything is locked upfront, so the note itself doesn’t have margin calls or liquidations.

The interesting part is each COUPON and SHIELD position is an ERC-1155 token, so it can be moved, used as collateral, or plugged into other apps.

They already have Credit through Morpho and Omni through LayerZero built around that idea.

The full protocol is still on testnet for now, with 5k+ users and 48 note series so far.

The points pre-season is live too, rewards grow with how much of the protocol you use, and they carry into mainnet, follow @notesystems for updates.

Robinhood Chain already brought stocks onchain. Now Note Systems is trying to bring the financial products built around those stocks onchain too.

Robots are going to order robots for robots. Thats the moment the exponential gets steeper... and its coming.

Today humans are still the ones ramping the factories. Elon, Figure and the Chinese all say the same thing. Robots will be maybe the largest physical product ever built, in scale and TAM. All of them are ramping production as fast as they can.

That first phase is exponential on its own. 

The next phase is the recursive one, the same loop agents already run in software. Robots will order more robots. Those robots build the next ones, and the loop stops waiting for us altogether...
